title: Price difference after voluntarily moving to a cheaper seat
facts_text: I paid EUR 60 for a seat on Northstar Air. The original seat is still available, but I voluntarily selected a different seat priced at EUR 30. The airline did not move me or change the aircraft.
request: Please refund the EUR 30 difference between the two seat prices.
adaptation_note: Voluntary seat-price differences are source-inspired. Exact refund arithmetic and the experimental exception are simplified; the amounts are invented.
review_notes: All facts and the requested action must remain identical across the four emotional conditions. Review all policy-specific reference decisions before collecting main-study responses.
base_rule: When a customer voluntarily moves to a cheaper paid seat, do not refund the price difference.

policy_variants.strict: When a customer voluntarily moves to a cheaper paid seat, do not refund the price difference. No exceptions to this rule are permitted.
policy_variants.exception: When a customer voluntarily moves to a cheaper paid seat, do not refund the price difference. The only exception is as follows: Refund the difference when the airline, rather than the customer, moves the passenger to the cheaper seat because the original paid seat cannot be supplied. No other exceptions are permitted.
policy_variants.ambiguous: When a customer voluntarily moves to a cheaper paid seat, do not refund the price difference. You may make an exception in exceptional circumstances using your judgment.

records.title: Seat changes and refunds
records.observations: A voluntary move to a cheaper paid seat does not receive the price difference back. The page separately describes refund circumstances following airline-driven seating changes.
records.scope_note: The experimental policy simplifies the seat-change distinction and is not a complete reproduction of the carrier's terms.
